on_south_pinnacle.blurb: South Pinnacle is a compact dolomite cliff at Old Baldy, the first wall you meet when working down the trail past the pinnacle. It holds 13 routes, almost all bolted sport lines with a single trad line. The grades start around 5.8 and 5.9, but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.13, with a couple of very hard lines at the top end, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners. Several of the routes here are well-regarded local standouts, and the afternoon sun makes it pleasant in cooler weather. The cliff has been getting steadily busier each year.

on_the_wall_of_shadows.blurb: The Wall of Shadows is one of the sectors at The Swamp, a newer cliff area developed by local climbers. It carries 13 routes: ten bolted sport lines and three trad lines. Grades run from easy 5.5 and 5.6 climbs up to 5.12, but most routes cluster in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it is best for climbers comfortable on steeper, sustained bolt-clipping. The wider Swamp cliff is south-facing with heavy tree cover and plenty of shade in the crevices. Grading across the area tends to feel on the generous side.

on_f_central_wall.blurb: Central Wall is one of the lettered sectors along the single long cliff line at Mount Nemo, near Burlington, and is divided by a big gully in the middle. It has 12 routes here, eight sport and four trad. The spread is lopsided: a handful of easy trad lines and short moderates, then a cluster of 5.12 sport climbs, with only a few routes in between. A well-known overhanging 5.11 sport line is the sector's classic. Reach the base by walking up or down the gullies and use the numbered plates along the foot of the cliff to find your route.

on_long_wall.blurb: Long Wall is a south-facing sandstone cliff at Pass Lake, east of Thunder Bay along Highway 587. Of its 12 routes, eight are bolted sport lines, three are trad and one is a top rope. Grades span the 5.7 to 5.12 range, with the heart of the wall in the 5.10s and low 5.11s. The walk from the car is almost nothing, around half a minute, and you can reach the top of the cliff to set up anchors. Sun on the face makes it a good early-season choice.

on_icebreakers_area.blurb: The Icebreakers Area is a group of frozen-waterfall and mixed lines in the Kama Bay zone on the north shore of Lake Superior, near Nipigon. It holds 12 routes: nine ice climbs and three mixed. Ice grades run from WI3 up to WI6, concentrated in WI4 and WI5, while the mixed lines reach around M7. It is a steep, serious venue with sustained climbing, and descents are usually by rappel from trees, so carry two ropes and plenty of screws. Kama Bay is quieter than neighbouring Orient Bay, though the approaches are longer and less travelled.
